items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: I used to fill in for Milt Hinton when Milt couldn’t make a gig... So when I couldn’t make the gig, Milt played the gig.

ctx.x: It seems like it’s an expensive proposition to go out and hear jazz sometimes.

It is. It’s very expensive. If you don’t put a hundred bucks in your pocket, you might not have enough, to take your wife out, just to go to the club, not to have dinner and all that. So it’s pretty expensive. And I remember Pearl Bailey told — I used to fill in for Milt Hinton when Milt couldn’t make a gig or something like that I would go to Jordan’s say for instance with Pearl. She was so wonderful to be with. And she would say that it’s a shame that jazz musicians are kind of pricing themselves out of the…
Do you think that’s the scene happening today? Do you think musicians are pricing themselves out?
